name: Pro-Europeanism
summary: Pro-Europeanism favours European integration, holding that pooling sovereignty in shared institutions secures peace, prosperity, influence and common values for European states. It is mainly a centrist, liberal-democratic outlook spanning centre-right, liberal, green and social-democratic parties, which differ on economics and social issues but agree on supranational cooperation. Strands range from federalists seeking a federal Europe to supporters of looser cooperation.
scope: The mainstream pro-EU outlook as expressed since the Schuman Declaration of 1950 and in the EU's own stated aims and values, as carried by the main pan-European party families (EPP, Renew, S&D, Greens/EFA, Volt). Excludes Euroscepticism, non-EU pan-European projects and any single national party's wider platform. Because the ideology is narrow, answers on economic and social questions are low-confidence inferences from its liberal-democratic, market-and-social-cohesion character.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Social progress and cohesion are EU aims and centre-left pro-Europeans back wage floors, but "substantially" is contested across the centre-right members of the family.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The EU pairs a highly competitive market economy with social goals, and pro-Europeans split between liberal and social-democratic emphases.

public-ownership.rationale: The single market and competition rules treat markets as the default, so a typical pro-European leans against broad nationalisation, though socialist pro-Europeans dissent.

unions-good.rationale: Social progress and worker protections are part of the EU project and mainstream pro-European parties accept social partnership with unions.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The EU is widely seen as a regulatory power (single market rules, competition, data and consumer protection), which pro-Europeans cite as a benefit of integration.

cut-welfare.rationale: Social cohesion and solidarity are stated EU aims, so a typical pro-European rejects welfare cuts as a goal, though centre-right members are more austere.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The EU stresses fundamental rights and personal data protection, so adherents lean against broad surveillance, with security-minded exceptions.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The EU's non-discrimination and equality commitments lead mainstream pro-Europeans to accept legal limits on hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Pro-Europeans stress representative democracy, rule of law and checks, which runs against bypassing gridlock through a strong leader.

state-harmful.rationale: The ideology is built on institutions, treaties and courts and holds that they secure peace and rights, so it rejects the claim that the state is harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Mainstream European centrist parties favour tight gun control, but the position is not part of pro-Europeanism itself.

empower-police-military.rationale: Pro-Europeans back common defence cooperation but are split on funding police and military authority generally.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Pro-European parties differ widely on sex work and the ideology is indifferent.

decide-locally.rationale: Pro-Europeanism favours moving decisions up to a European level; subsidiarity exists in EU law, but the statement as worded favours local over national decisions, which cuts against integration.

traditional-family.rationale: Christian-democratic and liberal pro-Europeans disagree on this, so adherents are genuinely split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The EU Charter bars discrimination and the typical pro-European, particularly in liberal, green and social-democratic parties, supports it, while EPP conservatives are split.

more-religion-public.rationale: The EU's secular institutional identity and pluralist values lean against a larger public religious role, with Christian-democratic dissent.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Gender equality is an EU principle but pro-Europeans do not agree on the social-construction claim.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pro-Europeans value national and shared European culture alike ("united in diversity"), so they are split on emphasis.

gradual-change.rationale: Schuman's declaration builds Europe through concrete steps creating de facto solidarity rather than a single sweeping plan, and integration proceeds through established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Free movement and openness are core to the project, and centrist pro-Europeans typically resist cutting immigration, though EPP voices want tighter external control.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Pro-Europeans hand binding powers to bodies above the nation, starting with Schuman's common High Authority (s1), and the EU's own foreign policy favours multilateral solutions through the UN. No cited source speaks to the UN's powers directly.

free-trade.rationale: The single market and common trade policy are core EU aims and pro-Europeans typically present open trade as beneficial.

nation-first.rationale: Pro-Europeanism rests on putting shared European interests above narrow national ones, with Schuman making war between nations materially impossible by pooling resources.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The EU aims to contribute to peace and security in the wider world and promote human rights, so adherents lean toward acceptance, but the ideology has no explicit line.

open-borders.rationale: The EU removes internal borders but maintains external ones, so pro-Europeans favour open borders within Europe, not everywhere.

limit-growth.rationale: The EU aims at competitive economy and sustainable development together, rejecting growth limits as such, though Green pro-Europeans dissent.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Protecting and improving the environment is a stated EU aim and pro-European parties generally back strong collective climate policy.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Pro-European parties and member states are divided over nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: The ideology is committed to treaties, democratic legitimacy and the rule of law, which are inconsistent with justifying revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Scholars note integration was elite-driven and a postfunctionalist public backlash followed, and adherents themselves dispute how much technocracy is acceptable.

central-planning.rationale: The EU aim is a competitive market economy, so pro-Europeans reject central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The EU commitment to market competition and social progress does not settle the question of ownership structure.

land-value-tax.rationale: There is no pro-European position on land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Taxation of inheritance divides pro-European centre-right and centre-left parties.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The customs union and single market oppose internal barriers, though the EU does use external tariffs, so adherents lean against protectionism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The EU does have industrial policy, yet adherents split between market-liberals and interventionists.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The EU aims at a market economy and monetary union with the euro, which is incompatible with abolishing money and wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Economic and monetary union with a common currency is a stated EU aim, requiring the European Central Bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Social partnership exists in Europe but state-recognised bodies fixing wages and prices is not a pro-European aim.

one-party-rule.rationale: The EU rests on representative democracy and pluralism, so pro-Europeans reject single-party rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Representative democracy is a founding value of the EU and a condition for membership, making adherents committed democrats.

direct-votes.rationale: The EU is built on representative democracy, and centrist pro-Europeans tend to distrust referendums, as in Brexit, though federalists favour some direct participation.

workers-councils.rationale: Pro-Europeanism operates through parliaments and treaty institutions, not councils.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equality before the law is a stated EU value, which is at odds with natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Schuman's goal was lasting peace, but pro-Europeans do not formally take a pacifist line on all political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: The project began to make war between France and Germany unthinkable and materially impossible, so it rejects war as ennobling. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

separate-church-state.rationale: The EU's secular institutions and rights-based values lean toward separation, though Christian-democratic adherents dissent.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: EU law rests on treaties and democratic agreement, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The ideology relies on independent public courts and shared institutions for justice and security.

military-superiority.rationale: Pro-Europeans emphasise collective security and peace, not unilateral superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Equality and non-discrimination plus free movement across a diverse union conflict with ethnically defined nations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Schuman approach rests on shared interests and solidarity rather than class conflict as the driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The EU stresses equal rights before the law and cohesion, but not equal outcomes as a goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No pro-European position and parties differ.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Schuman frames Europe on solidarity and common interests, which leans against self-interest as itself a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The EU Charter foregrounds individual rights, so adherents lean against putting duties before rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The EU aims to protect the environment but pro-Europeans are not committed on intrinsic value.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Pro-Europeanism champions prosperity and progress through a modern industrial and single-market economy.

human-enhancement.rationale: The ideology is indifferent and adherents divide.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Democratic accountability and rights protections lean against handing government decisions to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Privacy rights favour encryption while security-minded pro-Europeans seek access, so adherents are split.

restore-past-order.rationale: Pro-Europeanism is a forward-looking project of building new institutions to overcome Europe's past.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Integration is justified by its outcomes, but the project is also an explicit political ideal, so adherents are split.

direct-action.rationale: The ideology works through elections, parliaments and treaty procedures.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Pro-Europeanism is a modern, industrial, market-based project and has nothing in common with primitivism. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A single market with specialisation and exchange is the core economic project.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The EU's social aims are solidarity and cohesion, but goods are distributed through markets plus welfare, not by need alone.

production-for-use.rationale: The EU stresses a competitive market economy and profit-driven business, which opposes the statement's premise.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The ideology accepts competitive markets and does not hold that profit is exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: It rejects class dictatorship; democracy and rule of law are its founding values. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

collective-farming.rationale: The EU supports a market economy with private farming under its common agricultural policy.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The founding rationale is that economic integration among capitalist states makes war impossible, the opposite claim.

taxation-theft.rationale: Pro-Europeans fund common institutions and social cohesion through taxation and see it as legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberals within the camp agree, but Christian democrats and social democrats qualify it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The EU Charter protects individual rights but also recognises collective and social commitments, so adherents lean against the exclusive claim.

conscription.rationale: Pro-European states differ widely on conscription and the ideology is silent.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Pro-Europeans prize voting, representation and voice in common institutions as the check on power.

state-as-business.rationale: The ideology treats the state as a democratic, rights-bound community, not a business with customers.

media-academia-power.rationale: This is a populist claim not found among pro-Europeans, who generally trust media and universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equality and non-discrimination are EU principles, which reject racial hierarchy. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

organic-representation.rationale: Representative democracy through parties and the European Parliament is the EU's model.

total-state.rationale: Rights, rule of law and market economy conflict with a state directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The project aims to overcome nationalism rather than revive a nation, and Schuman cites past failures of nationalism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The project replaces conquest with pooled institutions to secure peace.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Legitimate authority rests on treaties, law and democracy, not oaths between lords and followers. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

bound-labor.rationale: Free movement of workers and individual rights are core to the project. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Pro-Europeans are mainstream liberal rationalists and generally reject this relativist claim.

universal-morality.rationale: The EU Charter proclaims universal rights and values, though adherents do not take a position on moral epistemology.

single-common-good.rationale: Scholars describe integration as bargaining among competing interests, so adherents accept balancing rather than a single good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The ideology has no position and pro-European parties vary.

revive-national-language.rationale: The EU supports multilingualism, but revival of a language as the state language is not a pro-European concern.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Co-determination exists in parts of Europe, yet adherents divide between centre-left and centre-right.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education policy is outside the ideology and parties differ.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Pro-Europeans split between fiscal-rules hawks and stimulus advocates, as seen in euro crisis debates.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule of law and binding institutions are preferred to reliance on rulers' example.

force-without-un.rationale: Pro-Europeans value multilateralism but disagree about unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Both secular liberals and Christian democrats are within the camp.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Pro-European parties differ on welfare conditionality.

class-collaboration.rationale: Schuman's declaration stresses solidarity and shared interests, and EU social partnership favours cooperation over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The EU treats cultural diversity and heritage as something to protect.

dominated-front.rationale: Pro-Europeanism is aligned with the democratic West and its partnerships, not fronts against it.

workers-nation.rationale: It favours transnational cooperation over organisation along purely national lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Equality between women and men underpins all European policies.

ban-interest.rationale: A market economy and monetary union with a central bank cannot prohibit lending at interest. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equality before the law and non-discrimination are core EU principles.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Pro-Europeans see the state and EU as bound by law and democracy, not as a tool of class rule.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The EU aim of environmental protection and climate action leans against expanding fossil fuels.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: "United in diversity" and equality are EU themes, though integration is encouraged, so adherents lean against full assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: This conspiracy claim conflicts with EU values and no pro-European source advances it. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

proportional-representation.rationale: Most pro-European parties accept proportional systems, as in European Parliament elections, but the position is not core.

national-mission.rationale: Pro-Europeans prefer cooperation and shared institutions over national missions, though some see Europe's model as exportable.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Equality between women and men is a stated principle, though the structural claim is contested among adherents.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Pro-Europeans defend institutions against populist critiques of corrupt elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Human dignity and equal rights under the Charter reject eugenic policy. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The EU pursues social, environmental and economic aims beyond defence and property protection.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Non-discrimination and equality are core EU values. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The EU states that equality is equal rights for all citizens before the law and builds the Charter on non-discrimination.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: There is no pro-European position and adherents differ.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Pro-Europeans take no position and member states differ.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Freedom of religion is protected by the EU Charter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Member states differ and the ideology does not decide.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The statement belongs to Marxism-Leninism and conflicts with pro-European democratic values.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The EU stresses that its treaties are voluntarily and democratically agreed, and that democratic legitimacy underpins it.

trade-surplus.rationale: The EU promotes open trade and mutual benefit, not mercantilist surplus targets.

population-transfer.rationale: It conflicts with human rights, non-discrimination and free movement.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The project is explicitly designed to replace national rivalry with solidarity, though market competition is accepted.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Pro-Europeans value pluralism yet accept defending democracy, so adherents are split.

separated-powers.rationale: The EU's institutions, courts and parliament check one another and the rule of law is a stated value.

vanguard-party.rationale: The ideology holds to representative democracy and rejects a leading revolutionary party. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Solidarity is an EU aim but a priority to the poor is not a pro-European position.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The EU frames diversity as compatible with unity and treats free movement as a strength.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The EU relies on elections and appointments, although citizens' assemblies appear in some pro-European proposals.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rights and rule of law are core values and not to be suspended, though security-minded members accept limits.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A competitive market economy favours market prices over fixed maximums.

party-controls-media.rationale: Democratic pluralism and fundamental rights oppose government control of the media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Pro-Europeans hold to democratic civilian control, not party command. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: This is a radical-democratic proposal absent from pro-Europeanism.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Pro-European parties vary in internal discipline and the ideology is silent.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Schuman proposed placing coal and steel under a supranational High Authority with binding decisions as the first step to a federation, which is the core pro-European position.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Parliamentary democracy with checks is the preferred model, so concentrating command in the head of state is disfavoured.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The ideology has no ecclesiastical position.

clerical-rule.rationale: Democracy and rule of law rule out clerical rule. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The pro-European approach seeks peace by cooperation among states, not revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Fundamental rights including expression are core EU values.

recall-officials.rationale: Pro-Europeans take no position and parties differ.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Pro-Europeans favour collective security and cooperation among allies.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Market economy with property and freedom of contract rule this out.

people-in-arms.rationale: Cooperative defence and professional forces are the norm, with no support for replacing armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The ideology has no such moral claim, so adherents lean against it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: This populist claim is rejected by mainstream pro-Europeans.

death-penalty.rationale: Rights-based EU values and the Charter commitment to human dignity lead adherents to oppose capital punishment, and abolition is expected of member states.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality is an EU principle and mainstream pro-Europeans favour it, though Christian democrats vary.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The EU's scientific and secular outlook leads adherents to reject creationism in public schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The ideology has no position and parties differ.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Open, equal and inclusive principles lean toward residence or birth-based citizenship over descent only.

minority-language-support.rationale: "United in diversity" and the EU's respect for linguistic diversity fit support for minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Charter protects religion and equality before the law, so adherents are split.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Pro-European parties disagree on debt cancellation.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: This is Mill's view and not specific to pro-Europeanism.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A market-economy ideology rejects transforming the property system as a condition of independence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Federalists favour a convention for a European constitution, but adherents differ on constitution rewriting generally.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Democracy and fundamental rights are founding values and not tradeable for growth. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Schuman named the development of Africa as an essential task of a united Europe, and the EU is a large aid donor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Pro-Europeans favour collective security through alliance, though some, like French federalists, back a European deterrent.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: No position, and the EU's own presidency models vary.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Economic and monetary union with an independent ECB focused on price stability is a stated EU aim.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The peace-through-compromise logic of the project leans against refusing territorial compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The EU's social market economy aims combine property with cohesion, though liberals qualify this.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: No pro-European position on Soviet characterisation.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Protecting the environment is a stated aim, and the precautionary principle is enshrined in EU environmental law.

collective-defense.rationale: EU aims include contributing to peace and security and mutual assistance; most adherents support collective defence, though neutral members add nuance.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Pro-Europeans are divided; Christian democrats oppose it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Many pro-European states have symbolic heads of state, but no position is documented.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Peaceful, consent-based politics leans against using military force on regions.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Pro-Europeans accept varied levels of autonomy within unions, as in multi-speed integration.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Equality before the law and democratic legitimacy conflict with a sacred ruler. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Social cohesion aims lean toward progressive taxation, though liberals differ.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule of law is a founding EU value and courts bind states and institutions.

space-expansion.rationale: Europe has a space programme but the ideology has no position on it being central.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The EU does mix institutions, but adherents hold no view on the classical doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Democratic pluralism and equality oppose leader cults. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Pro-Europeans reject aggression but accept lawful state coercion and collective defence, so an absolute non-aggression rule is not their position.

common-currency.rationale: Economic and monetary union with the euro is a stated aim of the EU and a central pro-European policy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Schuman's declaration founded integration on ending Franco-German rivalry, and the EU's values rest on respect for borders and rule of law, so ethnic territorial claims are opposed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Freedom of religion and human rights are core stated EU values, so punishing religious exit is rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: Equality between women and men and individual freedom are stated EU values, which conflict with legal compulsion to cover.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Schuman presents integration as a political act of will, though concrete economic solidarity is its method; adherents are not materialists in the Marxist sense.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rule of law and democracy with fundamental rights are stated EU values, which means courts and institutions do constrain majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Equality between women and men is a stated EU value and centre-left and liberal families back balanced representation, but mandated near-parity is contested on the centre-right.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The single market and open trade are core aims, so a closed autarkic bloc is the opposite of the outlook.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: EU trade policy states that it aims for high labour and environmental standards and its agreements contain trade and sustainable development rules.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Democracy and the rule of law are core stated values and integration was built by treaty, so armed revolutionary action is opposed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Adherents are split: EU anti-discrimination law permits some positive action, but the EU has no settled line on racial preferences.

delink-world-market.rationale: The EU's trade policy seeks integration of poor countries into the world market through trade agreements and sustainable development, the opposite of delinking.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The EU's stated values include non-discrimination and equality, so a general freedom to discriminate is rejected.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Respect for human rights and the rule of law is a founding EU value, entrenched in the Charter of Fundamental Rights and the treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: The EU founding values include democracy and representative government, not hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: EU decision-making relies on qualified majorities, so dissenting states are bound without consent in most areas.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The EU values include representative democracy, with the Parliament as co-legislator.

native-born-offices.rationale: Non-discrimination and free movement of citizens contradict reserving offices to the native born.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The Schuman Declaration aims to make war between European states materially impossible.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The EU values are presented as universal human rights, not civilization-specific.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Democracy and rule of law, core EU values, require civilian control of the military.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The EU's stated values include parliamentary democracy, and the European Parliament co-decides its budget.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Its founding aim is peace and its values stress democracy and sovereign equality of members.

democratic-peace.rationale: Schuman presented pooled coal and steel as making war between France and Germany materially impossible, and the EU lists democracy and peace together among its aims.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Equality, non-discrimination and respect for minorities are stated EU values, so the claim of a minority conspiring against the nation is rejected.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Pooled sovereignty and the supremacy of binding supranational institutions over national choices is the core of the outlook.

religious-nation.rationale: The EU states equality and pluralism as its values and defines belonging through shared institutions and values, not religion.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The EU stresses unity in diversity and multilingualism, a stance that rejects purging loanwords.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Human dignity, equality and the rule of law are stated EU values, and holocaust denial is criminalised in many member states.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Equality and non-discrimination are stated EU aims.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Democracy and pluralism are among the stated EU values.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Freedom of expression and religion are stated EU values and blasphemy penalties conflict with them.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Schuman presented European development of Africa as a joint task, not a metropolitan enterprise; modern pro-Europeanism is anti-colonial.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Democracy and the rule of law are the EU's basis, so religious law is no ground for removing rulers by force.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Equality is an EU aim, but the family spans centre-right and centre-left and takes no common view.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Non-discrimination is an EU value, but this is a national competence and adherents differ.

assisted-dying.rationale: National competence and a family split across religious and liberal parties.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Pro-Europeanism is a centrist outlook spanning left and right families, so it is split on this.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Tolerance, equality and non-discrimination are stated EU values.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Democracy as stated in EU values means authority comes from the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Member states differ, with France strict and others permissive, and no EU rule exists.

social-market-economy.rationale: The EU aims at a social market economy with competition rules and social cohesion.

rich-first.rationale: EU cohesion and solidarity aims favour spreading prosperity, though the Schuman Declaration speaks of concrete step-by-step achievements.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Most members are NATO or EU-defence members and the family favours alignment, though neutral members exist.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The outlook rests on an open single market and conventional banking; user-owned interest-free credit is not an EU aim, and the inference is from its market character.

property-franchise.rationale: The EU's stated values include democracy, equality and universal citizens' rights, which exclude wealth-based voting.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The EU stresses freedom and pluralism of the media, but adherents split between liberal and social-democratic views on ownership concentration.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The rule of law is among the EU's stated founding values, and the Union is built on treaties and law applied by courts.

racial-franchise.rationale: The EU's stated aims and values include equality and non-discrimination, which exclude any racial or ethnic limit on political rights.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency and open decision-making are EU aims and pro-Europeans favour them as an answer to the democratic deficit, though the sources give only the general value.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The EU's stated values include freedom, equality and non-discrimination, which exclude legal limits on marriage by religion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Non-discrimination and respect for minorities are stated EU values, so deliberate avoidance of shops of one religious minority is rejected.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The EU states equality and non-discrimination as core values, and mainstream pro-European party families back open service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The EU's stated values include freedom of religion and pluralism, so a state promoting atheism is contrary to them.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Pro-European liberal-democratic values rest on the rule of law and state policing, so abolition is far outside the outlook.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The EU is built on pooled sovereignty and consensus, and EU institutions favour inclusive arrangements, but adherents do not address divided societies directly.

term-limits.rationale: Not an integration issue; pro-European parties are split and it is a national matter.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: EU equality values favour equal access, but religious institutions are outside EU competence and pro-Europeans do not take a common view.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Equality between women and men is a stated EU value and mainstream pro-European parties support equal spousal authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: EU citizens living in another member state have a treaty right to vote in local and European elections there; extending it to all foreign residents is an inference and varies by party.

rent-control.rationale: Housing is a national competence and pro-European families split, with social democrats and greens favouring caps and liberals and centre-right opposing them.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Pro-Europeans are divided between supporters of NATO nuclear sharing and disarmament-minded greens and social democrats; the ideology itself takes no line.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The social market economy aims to balance enterprise and cohesion, but liberals and social democrats within the family disagree on how far income should favour work over capital.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Gender equality is an EU value but pro-European families do not share a view on the social construction of sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: This is an academic feminist debate on which the ideology takes no position; party families differ.

culture-before-state.rationale: The project built institutions first and let a shared culture follow, as Schuman's step-by-step economic solidarity shows.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The single market guarantees free movement of capital and establishment across borders and non-discrimination, which excludes reserving economic life for a national majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The ideology favours cross-border cooperation and regional diversity within existing states; merging regions by ethnicity is not part of it and cuts against shared borders.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Pro-Europeans span centre-right and left; EU competition rules favour liberalisation while the social model backs public services.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The EU's subsidiarity principle gives some local weight, but it favours governance, not confederal decision rules.

person-over-state.rationale: The EU's stated founding values start with human dignity and individual freedom, placing the person before the community.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The EU's stated values include equality and non-discrimination, which stand against organising by race.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The EU's stated values rest on equality and diversity, and it protects many languages inside shared institutions; pro-Europeans reject defining the nation by language and history.

communal-electorates.rationale: Equal rights for all citizens before the law is a core EU value, which is hard to square with separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Pro-Europeans warn of outside interference, but the outlook stresses cooperation and shared sovereignty, and a plot to partition one's country is a nationalist framing.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The EU's aims include protecting the environment and sustainable development, and carbon pricing is a standard EU tool, though parties differ on how far to rely on it.

future-generations.rationale: The EU treaty aims include sustainable development of the Earth and protection of the environment, which is a commitment to hand on a sound planet.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The EU stresses equality between women and men, not distinct female values; green and social-democratic strands lean to agree and liberal and centre-right strands do not.

capital-controls.rationale: Free movement of capital is part of the internal market, and the profile backs the single market and free trade.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The EU's aims include a social market economy and social partners' dialogue, which supports bargaining while competences remain national.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Pro-Europeanism is gradual, institution-building and liberal-democratic, and rejects overthrowing state institutions.

sacred-nation.rationale: Pro-Europeanism pools sovereignty and sets common European values above national exceptionalism, so sacralising the nation is contrary to it.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Common Agricultural Policy, a core EU policy, has long supported farm incomes through price support and direct payments, and mainstream pro-Europeans back it, though liberals favour reform.

ban-fgm.rationale: The EU states respect for human dignity and equality among its founding values, and the EU institutions have repeatedly called for banning FGM.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The EU's founding values rest on representative democracy and the rule of law, leaving no official lawmaking role for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The EU promotes sustainable development, but also stresses freedom as a founding value, and pro-Europeans differ on how to balance them.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Integration requirements are set nationally and pro-Europeans are split, with some supporting language tests and others opposing them as exclusionary.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Pro-Europeans span left and right and the EU leaves labour-union rules to member states.

voter-id.rationale: Voting rules are national and pro-Europeans disagree on identity checks.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The EU's stated values include equality and the rule of law, which fit equal legal treatment of religious interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: EU values go beyond elections to rule of law and rights, so a procedural-only test is too thin for most adherents.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The EU's democracy and rule-of-law values weigh against blanket shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Adherents differ on economics, so on replacing welfare with a negative income tax they are split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equality and democracy are stated EU values, and equal political rights for women are settled in its member states.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Equality between women and men is a stated EU aim, carried out partly through dedicated bodies.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The EU states its aims as peace, human rights and the rule of law, and pro-Europeans broadly back international courts for leaders who commit atrocities.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Equality between women and men is among the EU's stated values, so pro-Europeans favour guaranteeing it in self-government arrangements.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The EU aims at a competitive social market economy, and the pro-European centre rejects planned economies.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Pro-Europeans are split, with some backing referendums on territory and others, including most EU governments, defending existing borders.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The EU's stated values include the rule of law and human dignity, and the EU opposes the death penalty and killing without trial.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The aims and values of the EU rest on representative democracy and the rule of law, with parties and civil society as essential.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The EU's single market and competition rules aim to prevent special advantages, and state aid is restricted.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Pro-Europeanism seeks to pool national sovereignty, so adherents are split on how patriotism relates to worker-focused politics.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The EU's founding values of democracy and the rule of law are incompatible with one-party communist rule.

missingStatements.text: A single currency shared by several countries is better than separate national currencies.
missingStatements.rationale: Economic and monetary union with the euro is a stated aim of the EU and a central pro-European policy.

missingStatements.text: People should be free to live, work and study in any country of a continental union without a visa.
missingStatements.rationale: Freedom of movement without internal borders is an explicit EU aim and defining pro-European benefit.
missingStatements.declined: Free movement is covered loosely by open-borders and pool-sovereignty; too specific to one union.

missingStatements.text: Democratic countries that meet shared standards should be able to join a union of states as new members.
missingStatements.rationale: Schuman's High Authority was open to other European countries and the EU is open to further members.
missingStatements.declined: Enlargement of one union; covered by pool-sovereignty.

missingStatements.text: A united Europe should become a federation.
missingStatements.rationale: Schuman described the coal and steel community as a first step toward a European federation, though adherents split on how far to go.

notes: Pro-Europeans disagree among themselves on federalism versus intergovernmental cooperation, on fiscal rules, migration and enlargement. Economic and social answers mostly reflect the centrist, liberal-democratic family average and are low confidence.
